warning_signs_missed: 2026-05-29 — Finding a previous agency still logged into a new client's OnlyFans on day two is an onboarding control failure, not a lucky catch. We should have had a written access audit before go-live (who holds credentials, what gets rotated, who confirms) — and the same checklist run in reverse the day she left. Neither exists, which is why we also cannot say today whether ALTR still has access.

2026-05-30 — Subscribers dropping from 60-70/day to 4 in week one was the earnings story of this account and it was explained away in a single message. That day we should have set a written recovery target and a date, and scheduled a check-in against it. Instead the number was never revisited and she was left to infer performance from her own payouts.

2026-06-02 — Tagging '@sotom225' for the paid promo she was sold on, and never verifying that person made contact. Any introduction that produces zero messages within 48 hours should auto-escalate; the promo she specifically asked Derrek about simply never happened and nobody noticed.

2026-06-04/06-08 — She asked for content shoots and was told we were 'following up with them now' with photographers in Orlando. When that thread died it should have been closed honestly ('we don't have this yet'). An unanswered growth request from an engaged client is a bigger churn driver than a complaint, because she stops believing the ambitious version of the relationship exists.

2026-06-10 — Our first invoice was unpayable because of our own details. A billing error on invoice #1 should trigger a rail audit that day: pick one account, confirm it works with a $1 test, and freeze it. Instead we changed banks three more times in the next 21 days, which is a trust pattern that reads as instability to anyone who has been scammed before.

2026-06-11 — Her voice notes failed to upload and we did not notice; she caught it. Any client-supplied asset should have a confirmation-of-receipt step. This one incident quietly told her that if she does not check our work, nobody will.

2026-06-15 — The first billing dispute (commission on her own lives) was an at-risk flag, not an accounting query. It should have produced a written policy line in her contract terms that same week. It did not, so she recalculated the invoice herself again on 7/2 — a client doing our maths twice is a client already managing us.

2026-06-18 — Selling a video call with 'Duration : Not discussed' and letting the fan reach her before the brief. Every sold call/custom needs fan, amount, duration and exact promises recorded before the fan is told anything. She had already done the call by the time we told her about it.

2026-06-26 and 2026-06-28 — She reported the same leaks still live TWICE in three days. The second identical complaint is the single most reliable churn predictor in this book and it must trigger a same-day named-owner response with evidence (which URLs are down, which are pending, expected dates). Instead she got 'let me check on this with the team' and waited until 7/1 for a process explanation and never got confirmation on her actual links. She kept sending links until 7/5 and quit on 7/6.

2026-07-06 — The resignation itself. There is no trigger anywhere in our system that fires when a client says they are leaving, and no owner for an exiting client. Within an hour someone senior should have called her, thanked her, asked what went wrong, and agreed the final number — she had already offered to pay it in the same breath. Sixty days later that message has still never been answered.

2026-07-10 — Two ALTR functions posted routine content into a chat whose client had quit four days earlier. Automated cadences must be gated on account status; posting reel inspo at a departed client is the clearest possible proof to her that nobody is reading.

2026-08-02 — Our first post-churn contact was a request for paperwork so we could bill her. Any churned client should get an owner message before any collections message, and the final invoice should be issued unilaterally from our own OnlyFans records rather than made conditional on the departed client doing admin for us. That single sequencing choice is the reason both receivables are still uncollected.
top_fix: Build a churn trigger with a named owner: the moment a client says they are leaving, the account owner is notified and must make personal contact within 24 hours — before any invoice, request or automated cadence goes out — and all recurring posts to that chat are suspended. Everything else here follows from its absence. Concretely and this week: open message id 316 and write down the number she volunteered, issue the 7/1-7/7 invoice unilaterally from ALTR's own OF records with a 14-day pay-by date, deliver it once off-Telegram (SMS 407-587-9986, email Hannahchamberss2022@gmail.com, or a warm ask via Vale who referred her and is still a client), and in the same message do the offboarding we never did — confirm ALTR's OF access is revoked, hand over or delete the Facebook page we told her lives in 'our database', and tell her to change 'Gymgirl22!' and 'Bella_marie22!' because both are still sitting in this chat. If that is not done by 2026-09-11, write the receivable off and close the account; four identical weekly reports have produced zero actions and a fifth will not be different.
